items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: I know what you mean when you listen to Son House and Charley Patton and all that... I really dove into that [Mississippi Delta guys, like Son House and Robert Johnson...]

ctx.x: That’s such a great band, and I realized one day that I wasn’t the blues player that I needed to be to really play that band right. I played okay, but I wasn’t a great blues player and I feel like every jazz musician has to be a good blues player. So I put it upon myself to be more informed and be a better blues player and maybe study where it came from. And one of the things I went to was the Mississippi Delta guys, like Son House and Robert Johnson and those guys, and I really dove into that. And I got to where…

I love that statement you just made, being a better jazz player through being a better blues player. I know what you mean when you listen to Son House and Charley Patton and all that, it takes a while to understand that. At first I remember thinking well they just played five measures on the one chord, and do they know they did that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
And there’s only three beats in that bar.
